doc.title: Howard Levy interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 11, 2025

title: Writing the musical memoir
summary: He began writing diary-like stories decades ago and seriously during the pandemic, recalling details cinematically; the 450-page book had stories cut.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: I saw that and I was going to bring that up. And that takes a bit of time, doesn’t it?

Oh man. You know I started writing some of these stories literally years ago, maybe twenty years ago, more like diary entries. Like I remember this important thing from my life and I’m going to type it out. And I put a few of them on my first website maybe even like thirty years ago. And then during the pandemic, when all of us had way too much time on our hands and you know the alternative was, you know, jump out a window somewhere or be really productive and really work on stuff. Well I did a lot of stuff during the pandemic. A lot of recording for people and I did a whole series of broadcasts from my home with a multi-camera thing and raised a whole bunch of money for the Greater Chicago Food Depository. I did a lot of stuff during the pandemic. But I also

started really seriously writing my memoir. Because when you sit around by yourself and you don’t have the usual musical interaction, or even personal interaction with people, I found that I could go into my memory and just remember things cinematically, really. I remember, as I thought about it more and more, I just started remembering all these tiny details, like colors and smells and all sorts of things like that. So when we finally got the book into its final form I had to edit out probably like a good ten or fifteen of the stories. It would have just been too long.
That is one of the hardest things to do, you’ve got a wealth of good material and something’s got to go here.
Yeah, yeah. It was just, the book is over 450 pages long and I just didn’t want to make it any fatter than that. You know I didn’t want to scare anybody.
